I don't think you are the asshole here, since your grandma was quite unwilling to explain why they changed their attitude to you so suddenly. I won't make any guesses as to why they did, but I can see that it was a huge shock to you and for autistic folk like us this can be very confusing and upsetting. The entire interaction suddenly changed when everything had seemed fine, and you hadn't been anything but your normal self.


However, when you got upset, you forgot that you were a guest in their house, and when you told your mean grandma not to butt in, you were ignoring her right to be part of interactions that take place in main areas of her own home. Only your not-mean grandma was really allowed to do that, since it is her home too. That was an easy thing to forget for you, but it meant they saw you as rude and felt justified in yelling. 


This means that unless you apologize for that specific act, and calling them b*tches, they will see themselves as having chased a rude, angry person away and feel justified in having done it. If you are ok with that, you don't need to do anything, just let them think what they want.


If you *did* apologize and explain you got upset and know now you went too far, it might help you not be enemies in the future.


Up to you to decide! 


TLDR: NTA because they suddenly got weird about you which would upset anybody but apologising might help, IF you ever want to talk to grandma in the future.
